problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,3]\times [0,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=5x{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}-3xy-2x.
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[2,\,1]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{1}=[$ | $0$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-1}} |  |  |
worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(5x{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}-3xy-2x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(5x{y}^{2}-5{x}^{2}-3xy-2x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10x+5{y}^{2}-3y-2 \\ 10xy-3x\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(-10x+5{y}^{2}-3y-2) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(10xy-3x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(-10x+5{y}^{2}-3y-2) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(10xy-3x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 & 10y-3 \\ 10y-3 & 10x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}-10 & 10y-3 \\ 10y-3 & 10x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-10x+5{y}^{2}-3y-2 \\ 10xy-3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with
${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}-10 & 10y-3 \\ 10y-3 & 10x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-10x+5{y}^{2}-3y-2 \\ 10xy-3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-10 & 10(1)-3 \\ 10(1)-3 & 10(2)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-10(2)+5(1)^{2}-3(1)-2 \\ 10(2)(1)-3(2)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-10 & 7 \\ 7 & 20\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-10)\cdot 20-7\cdot 7}[\begin{aligned}20 & -7 \\ -7 & -10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{249}[\begin{aligned}-498 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
